notes: Reference date 2018-02-24. New Parent Leave and NYS PFL took effect 2018-01-01, so both are in force; all other documents carry earlier version dates or copies from the 2017-18 reference year.
E33.0 Family Leave Policy holds no policy text of its own: it points to the FMLA page of HR (saved as 2018_05). The E-series governance pages carry long site-navigation lists, which hold no policy.

Faculty pay basis: 'All faculty are paid over 12 months', so faculty fall in the STD class '12 Month Employee & Less Than 12 Months Per Fiscal Year Employee Who is Paid Over 12 Months', paid 100% for the first 8 weeks; the special note on 9-month faculty concerns coverage over the summer only.

U8 paths: an employee who does not work in New York State is not eligible for NYS PFL and takes RIT New Parent Leave separately (full pay, primary 4 / secondary 2 weeks, block or intermittent, 'may be taken immediately following the disability period or birth'). The coded path is the NY-working member eligible for NYS PFL.

Not components: E17's paid leave of absence (only where 'the professional status of the individual and hence the university will be enhanced'); FMLA-equivalent care of other relatives (parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild) at the supervisor's discretion without job protection; the research-faculty one-year leave for externally funded research (E05). None is a leave a parent could take for the birth.
Calendar: E04 states semesters ('beginning with the fall semester'), length not stated -> calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. No component uses a term unit.

Chain, birth parent: STD absence 8 (job held up to 26) [STD childbirth pay 8 weeks at 100%, week 1 the waiting week paid by Salary Continuation; NY DBL within from week 2] -> NYS PFL leave 8 [PFL benefit 50% to NYAWW from its start; RIT New Parent Leave top-up to full pay for the first 4 weeks (primary) or 2 (secondary), in_lieu_of each other] ; FMLA 12 alongside from the start of the STD absence. Matches the fact sheet's chart (weeks 1-8 STD, 9-12 PFL + New Parent Leave, 13-16 PFL, weeks 1-12 FMLA).

Chain, non-birth parent: NYS PFL leave 8 from the birth [PFL benefit 50%; New Parent Leave top-up to full pay 4 weeks primary or 2 weeks secondary, in_lieu_of] ; FMLA 12 alongside from the start (domestic-partner FMLA-equivalent leave concurrent with FMLA). Salary Continuation (5 business days, family illness) and the discretionary unpaid family-illness leave after it are recorded but unlinked to the parental chain.

Cross-references not saved: the New York State Paid Family Leave page of the HR website (www.rit.edu/HumanResources/PFL), which holds the NYS PFL service eligibility rules; RIT's long-term disability plan document; E18.0 Faculty Leave for Professional/Career Development; E34.0 Military Leave; E01.0 Classification of Employment; E06.0, E07.0 (named in E04/E05, not leave-related); the Benefits Health and Wellness page of HR (E04 IV.C.5); the Domestic Partner Benefits page; the STD plan document/contract (fact sheet: 'the plan document/contract will be the final authority').

Source precedence: the fact sheet (summary) and the STD summary agree on the childbirth STD period (8 weeks) and on PFL following the STD period; the STD summary's '100% Supplemental Pay Period - the 8 weeks following the initial one week Waiting Period' describes a general disability; for a birth the summary states the disability is 'automatically 8 weeks' and the fact sheet's chart puts the waiting week inside those 8 weeks. Coded as the 8-week envelope (V4); a reading of 1 + 8 = 9 weeks at 100% would add one week to c2.
